newsitem.title: CANADA: Seagram's first-quarter earnings jump 8 percent.
newsitem.headline: Seagram's first-quarter earnings jump 8 percent.

text.p: Seagram Co. Ltd. on Wednesday reported sharply higher first quarter profits, reflecting improved results at its MCA Inc. entertainment division and a one-time gain.

The global entertainment and beverage concern, which raised its quarterly dividend by 10 percent, said net income for the three months ended Sept. 30 jumped to $166 million, or 45 cents a share, from $66 million, or 18 cents a share.
The results, however, included a gain of $39 million related to Seagram's sale of DuPont Co. warrants in July.
Quarterly revenues slipped to $2.94 billion from $2.97 billion.

Seagram Chief Executive Edgar Bronfman Jr. attributed the improved results to the success of the company's Crown Royal and Captain Morgan brands in North America and its Tropicana Dole Beverages sector.

"We were pleased with the spirits and wine (operating earnings) growth despite the revenue decline in Europe and Asia Pacific in the quarter," said Bronfman. "In addition, it is gratifying to see the realisation of benefits associated with our reengineering efforts."
The company said strong results in North America were offset by competitive pressures in Europe and Asia.

Bronfman said strong results at the MCA entertainment unit were driven by the success of two new theme park attractions, Terminator 2 at Universal Studios in Florida and the Jurassic Park ride at Universal Studios in Hollywood.
Seagram purchased 80 percent of MCA from Matsushita Electric Industrial Co. Ltd. last year for $5.7 billion.
Seagram said it raised its quarterly dividend to 16.5 cents a share from 15 cents.
